item.title: Analysis of Triggered Packet Streams: Stochastic Bounds on System Time under General Triggering Delays
item.description: arXiv:2610.40865v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many emerging communication systems increasingly involve devices that transmit packets in multiple causally dependent stages as part of an internal workflow, rather than waiting for receiver feedback. To analyze such systems, we recently introduced the $\mathrm{M^T/G/1}$ queue, in which primary customers arrive according to an exogenous Poisson process, and each triggers a secondary customer to join the queue after an independent random delay, called the \textit{triggering delay}. Our prior heuristic approximations assume identical exponential service times, and our matrix-analytic framework assumes exponential triggering delays. However, no exact analysis is available when both distributions are general. In this paper, we derive stochastic bounds, in the usual stochastic order, on the system-time distribution of each customer class under general triggering-delay and service-time distributions. The service times within each primary--secondary pair may be generally dependent. Using sample-path coupling and level-crossing arguments, we show that the stationary workload is stochastically sandwiched between those of two classical queues: a two-class $\mathrm{M/G/1}$ queue with independent Poisson arrivals (lower bound), and a batch-arrival $\mathrm{M^{[2]}/G/1}$ queue where each primary--secondary pair arrives simultaneously (upper bound). Notably, these bounds do not depend on the triggering-delay distribution, and they are asymptotically tight in the sense that the stationary workload converges in distribution to that of the lower- and upper-bound queues as the triggering delays diverge to infinity and converge to zero in probability, respectively. We translate these workload bounds into system-time bounds for each customer class. Simulation experiments support these bounds.
item.dc:creator: Mehran Rahnamania, Michel Mandjes, Farid Ashtiani

item.title: Martingale Representation in Counting-Process Filtrations via Poisson Embedding
item.description: arXiv:2610.40980v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit martingale representation for counting processes using the Poisson embedding, deriving the representation in their natural filtration from that of the underlying Poisson random measure. Our approach combines Poisson Malliavin calculus with the Clark-Ocone and Mecke formulas. We first characterize measurability with respect to the counting-process filtration through the structure of the Malliavin derivative. We show that any random variable measurable in the counting-process filtration is invariant with respect to the auxiliary mark on the acceptance region obtained from the Poisson embedding method and vanishes on the rejection region. We then prove that every square-integrable martingale in this smaller filtration consequently admits a unique stochastic integral representation with respect to the compensated counting process: the integrand is explicitly characterized as the conditional expectation of the Malliavin derivative, which identifies as the conditional effect of an additional accepted event on the terminal functional. Additionally, we define the mirroring counting process which counts the rejected events in the Poisson embedding procedure and we then provide an orthogonal decomposition of any martingale in the joint filtration of the accepted and rejected counting processes as a sum of a martingale in the counting filtration obtained by Poisson embedding and its mirroring martingale part on the rejected domain. Finally, we apply these results to general Hawkes processes constructed by Poisson embedding, obtaining a martingale representation and an explicit integrand formula in their natural filtration.
item.dc:creator: Caroline Hillairet, Thibaut Mastrolia, Anthony R\'eveillac

item.title: Strong solvability and its failure for critical SDEs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We revisit the construction of strong solutions to singular SDEs by compactness on Wiener space. For spatially varying diffusion coefficients, assuming sufficiently small form bounds on the drift and diffusion gradient, we use basic energy estimates and an extended compactness criterion for Wiener functionals to construct an approximation-independent stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. Both forward and inverse maps have local Sobolev moment bounds, and the resulting strong solutions are pathwise unique in a class of solutions satisfying a Krylov estimate. We also show that the endpoint critical condition $b\in L^\infty_tL^d_x$, together with $\mathrm{div } b=0$ does not guarantee the existence of a strong solution. For every $d\geq2$, we construct a SDE with a divergence-free drift in this class and an additive Brownian noise, started from the origin, has a weak solution unique in law, but no strong solution. The proof uses logarithmic rescaling to characterize strong solvability by whether the sample measures of an associated stationary diffusion are Dirac masses. Positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent, combined with random SRB theory, rules out this concentration and hence strong solvability.
item.dc:creator: Dejun Luo, Guohuan Zhao

item.title: Efficient Importance Sampling of Brownian Motion Avoiding Poissonian Obstacles for Long Time
item.description: arXiv:2610.41234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We design and analyze an efficient importance sampling estimator of the probability that, over a long time horizon, a Brownian particle avoids obstacles of a fixed radius placed according to an independent Poisson random field. Donsker and Varadhan identify the exponential decay rate of this probability as the optimal balance between the volume cleared of obstacles and the spectral cost of confinement, and the confinement results of Sznitman and Povel show that the particle survives by localizing its path in a ball of (roughly) deterministic radius but with a random center. This strategy makes direct Monte Carlo exponentially ineffective over long horizons, and makes a practical yet asymptotically optimal sampler non-trivial to design, since the sampler must track the random region swept out by the path. For every fixed dimension \(d\ge2\) and every fixed obstacle radius, we construct a sequential importance sampler that is unbiased and asymptotically optimal. The full algorithm has finite expected total work at every fixed horizon, and both its expected work and the coefficient of variation grow at most subexponentially with the time horizon. The method avoids repeatedly solving eigenvalue problems on the evolving explored regions and suits parallel implementation. Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency of the method.
item.dc:creator: Jose Blanchet, Paul Dupuis, Hao Liu

item.title: A Model for Fast Mining Blockchains
item.description: arXiv:2610.41312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a Markovian model for a blockchain mining process. In the limit where there is an infinite number of miners, the model satisfies a functional law of large numbers due to Barbour and Luczac (2008), leading to an infinite set of coupled ODEs characterising the blockchain heights. We show that the sequence of solutions to this system converges uniformly, to a limiting profile in an appropriate comoving frame. Utilising asymptotic arguments inspired by Brunet and Derrida (1997), we derive an explicit expression for the position of the travelling front, which exhibits a leading order logarithmic Bramson correction in time. For a finite number of miners, we further derive a correction to the travelling speed which is logarithmic in the number of miners. Finally, by application of a computation due to Ablowitz and Zeppetella (1979), we identify that, for a specific choice of the travelling speed, the Painlev\'e integrable, travelling wave solution of the Fisher-KPP equation with drift accurately matches our limiting profile. Our results are supported by numerical simulations.
item.dc:creator: Rhys Bowden, Cengiz Gazi, Jan de Gier, Peter Taylor

item.title: Cutoff for random Cayley graphs of finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.41347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the random walk on a Cayley graph of a finite group whose generators are chosen independently and uniformly at random. We show that, for every finite group, the walk exhibits cutoff with high probability whenever the number of generators is large compared with the logarithm of the order of the group but small compared with every positive power of it. The cutoff time is the time at which the expected entropy of the walk comes close to its maximum, and in general it depends on the structure of the group. This settles a conjecture of Aldous and Diaconis.
item.dc:creator: Haoran Zhu

item.title: Strong well-posedness for cyclic catalytic reaction--diffusion SPDEs with mutation and immigration
item.description: arXiv:2610.41400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study cyclic catalytic stochastic reaction-diffusion systems with mutation and immigration. The equations have square-root catalytic coefficients and spatially colored noise. Under a condition requiring the cyclic inward drift to dominate the corresponding noise covariance, we establish global strong well-posedness for nonnegative initial states. Our approach combines positivity-preserving approximations, uniform energy estimates, and a concave power entropy that controls the occupation of states near zero. These boundary estimates allow us to derive a Hellinger stability inequality for two synchronized weak variational solutions, yielding pathwise uniqueness directly in this solution class. We then use joint compactness of the approximating solutions and their driving noise, together with martingale identification and the Gyongy-Krylov criterion, to construct a probabilistically strong solution on the prescribed Wiener space.
item.dc:creator: Jie Xiong, Wen Xu

item.title: Tracy Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration
item.description: arXiv:2610.41416v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study sample covariance matrices formed from i.i.d., centered, isotropic random vectors $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \mathbb{R}^M$, whose coordinates are allowed to be dependent. We assume the random vectors satisfy a concentration bound for their quadratic forms $q_i^T A q_i$. Under this assumption, we establish edge universality and obtain the Tracy--Widom law for the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix after appropriate centering and scaling. In particular, our result removes the unconditionality assumption in existing edge universality results for log-concave ensembles~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.
item.dc:creator: Guangchen Chen, Xing Lyu

item.title: Invariant probability measures for path-dependent regime-switching processes
item.description: arXiv:2610.41515v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider stochastic functional differential equations with Markovian regime?switching on an (infinitely) countable state space. Via establishing the Feller prop?erty and contraction in L1-Wasserstein distance of the semigroup associated with the segment process, we show the existence and uniqueness of invariant probability measure. In order to cope with switching processes on an infinite state space, we de?velop a truncation method based on a new construction of order preserving coupling for Markov chains to generalize the estimation of exponential functionals for Markov chains with infinite states. The existing sharp estimation is only valid for Markov chains on a finite state space, as it fundamentally relies on the Perron-Frobenius theorem.
item.dc:creator: Jianrui Li, Jinghai Shao

item.title: Genetic weight of a mutant in a biparental Moran model with infinite selection
item.description: arXiv:2610.41650v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study, after Coron Le Jan (2024), the genetic contribution of a single strongly advantageous mutant in a biparental Moran model under infinite selection. We prove a functional limit theorem for the entire beneficial mutation spreading period: after normalization by \(\sqrt N\), the contributions carried by the advantaged and disadvantaged subpopulations converge jointly in law to a non-degenerate random multiple of an explicit deterministic profile. Randomness is generated during the initial microscopic growth of the mutant lineage and subsequently propagated through the population along a deterministic macroscopic trajectory. At the heart of this phenomenon is an eigenmode martingale that measures the imbalance between the mean genetic weight of the founding ancestor within the two classes; its limiting value provides precisely the random amplitude of the macroscopic profile and is characterized by a smoothing equation.
item.dc:creator: Camille Coron (MIA Paris-Saclay, INRAE), Olivier H\'enard

item.title: Bridging rough stochastic differential equations and rough semimartingales
item.description: arXiv:2610.41664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We bridge the gap between the mixed-moment theory of c\`adl\`ag rough stochastic differential equations (short:RSDEs), introduced by Friz, Hocquet and L\^e (2021) and extended to the c\`adl\`ag setting by Allan and Pieper (2026), and the theory of rough semimartingales (short:RSMs), introduced by Friz and Zorin-Kranich (2023), by investigating the intersection of these two theories for the first time. By introducing the concept of good solutions to RSDEs, solutions which are simultaneously both mixed-moment solutions and RSMs, we develop a solution concept, which allows for good control on both moment-based and pathwise properties of solutions. The well-posedness of good solutions is proven using a fixed point argument on the space of $L^{2}$-martingales by suitably leveraging previously known mixed-moment estimates. Based on these insights we further characterize a large class of good solutions of semi-linear RSDEs through a novel rough stochastic Duhamel's principle.
item.dc:creator: Jannis R. Dause, Peter K. Friz, Jost Pieper

item.title: First and second order firing statistics of large neuronal networks with community structure
item.description: arXiv:2610.41706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a discrete-time stochastic model for the spiking activity of a network of $n$ interacting neurons partitioned into $k$ communities. The interaction network is a random directed weighted graph generated by a Stochastic Block Model with $k+1$ edge types ($k$ intra-community, $1$ inter-community). Each edge is present independently with a probability that depends only on its type. When present, an edge carries a type-dependent deterministic weight scaled by $n^{-1}$, which is excitatory or inhibitory depending on an independent random sign. Given the interaction network, the spiking process is a stationary Markov chain. Our results describe how the network's community structure manifests itself in the first- and second-order statistics of this chain, as $n \to \infty$ with $k$ fixed. Representing these statistics as explicit functions of the random interaction network, we prove that, with high probability: (i) the vectors of mean firing activity and firing variances are approximated in supremum norm by deterministic vectors that are constant within each community, with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n}$; (ii) the off-diagonal part of the $0$-lagged firing covariance matrix is approximated in max norm, with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n^3}$, by a deterministic community-block matrix (constant on each block defined by a pair of communities), with block values determined by the unique solution to a $k \times k$ Stein matrix equation; (iii) in contrast, the $t$-lagged covariance matrix, for every lag $t \ge 1$, is approximated in max norm, again with an error of order $\sqrt{\log(n)/n^3}$, by a random matrix built from two components: a random matrix capturing the interaction network and a deterministic community-block matrix. Finally, we discuss conditions on the model parameters under which these limiting statistics enable the identifiability of the community structure.
item.dc:creator: Thiago H. N. Coelho, Daniel Figueiredo, Giulio Iacobelli, Guilherme Ost, Conrado C. Pinto

item.title: Critical fluctuations in the edge--triangle exponential random graph models
item.description: arXiv:2610.41781v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove quantitative limit theorems for the edge density $Q$ in the dense edge--triangle exponential random graph model at criticality and under parameter perturbations of order $n^{-1}$. At the fixed critical parameters $(\alpha_c,h_c),$ the centered fluctuations satisfy $n^{2/3}(Q-\mathbb{E} Q)\Rightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_0^2)$, with explicit variance $\sigma_0^2>0$. This disproves the quartic fluctuation conjecture of Bianchi, Collet and Magnanini (2024). Gaussian limits also hold $(\alpha_c+ \lambda/n,h_c + \gamma/n)$, except when the coefficients satisfy $-\frac{11}{16}+\frac{2}{9}(\gamma+\frac49\lambda)=0$. Under this linearity condition, the limiting laws of $\sqrt n(Q-2/3)$ have densities proportional to $\exp\{-81z^4/64+9\theta z^2/8\}$, where $\theta=-57/16+8\lambda/27$. We obtain a sharp $n^{-1/3}$ rate in $1$-Wasserstein distance for the Gaussian limits and an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound for the quartic limits. The proofs combine Stein's method for exchangeable pairs with conditional row estimates and a local Dobrushin contraction.
item.dc:creator: Song-Hao Liu, Qi-Man Shao, Hao Shi, Jing-Yu Xu

item.title: Localisation and delocalisation of the integer-valued membrane model
item.description: arXiv:2610.41925v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the integer-valued membrane model on boxes $[-L,L]^d\cap\mathbb{Z}^d$ with zero boundary conditions. We show that in dimension two the model is delocalised at sufficiently high temperature. More precisely, the variance at the origin is of order $L^2/\beta$, where $\beta$ is the inverse temperature. More generally, for every $\epsilon>0$ and all sufficiently small $\beta>0$, the logarithm of each Laplace transform lies between $(1+\epsilon)^{-1}$ and $1$ times its Gaussian counterpart. The temperature threshold is independent of $L$ and the test function. In dimensions three and four, we prove that the variance at the origin is bounded uniformly in the box size at every positive inverse temperature. Thus the integer constraint changes the order of fluctuations in these dimensions. The proofs use a modification of the Fr\"ohlich--Spencer argument in dimension two and a comparison with integer-valued Gaussian free fields in higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Alessandra Cipriani, Biltu Dan, Rajat Subhra Hazra

item.title: Maximum of the Two-Dimensional Directed Polymer in the Critical Window
item.description: arXiv:2610.41989v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $Z_N^{\beta_N}(x)$ denote the partition function of the two-dimensional directed polymer started at $x\in \mathbb{Z}^2$, in Gaussian environemnt, in the critical window, with parameter $\beta_N=\sqrt{(1-\vartheta/\log N)/R_N}$. Here $R_N\sim (\log N)/\pi$ is the truncated collision Green function at the origin for the simple random walk on $\mathbb{Z}^2$. Let $\mathfrak M_N$ denote the maximum of $\log Z_N(x)$ over $|x|_\infty\leq \sqrt{N}$. We prove that, for any $\vartheta\in \mathbb{R}$, in probability, $$\mathfrak M_N/\sqrt{\log N}\to 2\sqrt{2}\text{ as }N\to\infty.$$
item.dc:creator: Clement Cosco, Shuta Nakajima, Ofer Zeitouni

item.title: When is the deepest drawdown also the longest?
item.description: arXiv:2610.41990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Does the deepest drawdown take the longest to recover? For random walks with iid increments of positive finite mean, we find that the deepest and longest episodes are eventually distinct almost surely under light-tailed losses, but coincide with probability tending to one under heavy-tailed losses. More precisely, when losses have a finite exponential moment, the deepest episode's duration, relative to the longest among $n$ episodes, converges in probability to an explicit $\rho\in(0,1)$, while its descending duration rank is $n^{1-\rho+o_{\mathbb{P}}(1)}$. These limits hold for every fixed number of leading depths; in the Gaussian model, $\rho=1/2$, independently of drift and variance. The separation reflects the different exponential costs of reaching a large depth and sustaining a long episode. For regularly varying losses, a common large loss governs both depth and duration: the duration ratio tends to one almost surely, and for every fixed $k$, the $k$ deepest and $k$ longest episodes have the same indices in the same order with probability tending to one. For any $k_n\to\infty$ with $k_n=o(n)$, the proportion of common episodes among the $k_n$ deepest and $k_n$ longest converges in probability to zero in the light-tailed case and to one in the heavy-tailed case. These ranking laws also hold for completed drawdowns within a deterministic observation horizon.
item.dc:creator: Yinhao Wu

item.title: Stochastic processes on reductive homogeneous and symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.42025v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we present a method to effectively and efficiently provide pathwise approximations of the Riemannian Brownian motion on a reductive homogeneous space $M\cong G/H$ endowed with a $G$-invariant metric. This setting includes spheres, hyperbolic spaces, the space of symmetric positive-definite matrices, flag manifolds and Stiefel manifolds. The simulation is based on Wong--Zakai approximations of an appropriately chosen SDE in $G$ that is projected down onto $M\cong G/H$. The effectiveness lies in the fact that well-established results on the convergence rate of the Wong--Zakai equation immediately carry over to the homogeneous space thanks to Nash's embedding. The efficiency lies in the fact that explicit representations of the Wong--Zakai approximations can be obtained in this setting using the Lie exponential map.
item.dc:creator: Sonja Cox, Erwin Luesink

item.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2610.42059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sampling from the ferromagnetic $q$-state Potts model is a fundamental problem in statistical physics and approximate counting. Although computationally hard in the worst case, sampling is expected to be efficient throughout the high-temperature uniqueness regime of the model using the natural single-site Glauber dynamics. We establish fast mixing bounds for every $q$, in the full high-temperature regimes in the two central graph families on $n$ vertices. (1) For every $\Delta\ge 3$, the Potts Glauber dynamics mixes in $n\operatorname{polylog}(n)$ steps with high probability on a uniformly random $\Delta$-regular graph for all $\beta<\beta_u(q,\mathbb T_\Delta)$ where $\beta_u(q,\mathbb T_\Delta)$ is the uniqueness threshold on the $\Delta$-regular tree; (2) For every $d\ge 2$, the Potts Glauber dynamics has inverse spectral gap $n^{1+o(1)}$ on cubes or tori in $\mathbb Z^d$ for all $\beta<\beta_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ where $\beta_c(q,\mathbb Z^d)$ is the critical point on $\mathbb Z^d$. Both temperature thresholds are sharp as the Glauber dynamics slows down exponentially above them. These results overcome the challenge of bounding mixing times without access to correlation decay bounds in the presence of pinnings (i.e., without spectral independence or strong spatial mixing). For this purpose, our proof introduces a new dichotomy principle: throughout the high-temperature regime, any initial spin distribution is either such that its pinnings ensure good correlation decay, or Glauber dynamics escapes from that distribution quickly. We expect this kind of dichotomy to have further applications. As a demonstration, we also develop its analog for random-cluster dynamics and use it to prove that Swendsen-Wang dynamics on random $\Delta$-regular graphs mixes in $O(\log n)$ time throughout uniqueness. The results in this paper were arrived at with the assistance of ChatGPT 5.6 and 6.
item.dc:creator: Antonio Blanca, Reza Gheissari, Heehyun Park, Xusheng Zhang

item.title: Spectra of stochastic matrices with a Toeplitz interior
item.description: arXiv:2610.42072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For stochastic matrices of order $n$, the Karpelevi\v{c} region is the set of all possible eigenvalues. We study matrices whose first and last $m$ rows are arbitrary probability vectors, while the remaining middle rows come from one probability vector by successive cyclic shifts to the right, moving the last entry to the first position each time. As $m$ increases, their eigenvalue regions expand from the polygon spanned by the $n$th roots of unity. For $n\ge3$, they first equal the full Karpelevi\v{c} region at $m=\lceil(n-1)/4\rceil$. Reproducing all $n$ eigenvalues, counted with multiplicity, of every stochastic matrix of the same order requires $m=\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Thus, in even order $n\ge4$, retaining two consecutive rows with the Toeplitz pattern can exclude eigenvalue lists even when every possible eigenvalue occurs individually. The boundary of the Karpelevi\v{c} region consists of arcs joining roots of unity. We determine the least $m$ for which every point of each arc occurs as an eigenvalue in our family. For arcs whose nonreal points first become possible eigenvalues at order $n\ge4$, and for $m\ge1$ below this minimum, no point on the arc other than its endpoints occurs in the family. At the minimum, every point on the arc becomes attainable. At the smallest order $n\ge4$ at which a nonreal point on a boundary arc away from its endpoints can occur as an eigenvalue, that point determines the characteristic polynomial of every stochastic matrix of order $n$ having it as an eigenvalue. Further results describe the smaller regions and the angles at which their boundaries approach roots of unity.
item.dc:creator: Brecht Verbeken, Vincent Ginis

item.title: Dirichlet form approach to stochastic thin-film equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.42086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The thin-film equation describes the evolution of a thin liquid film driven by capillarity and limited by viscosity. For sufficiently small film heights, thermal fluctuations may not be neglected. Since the thin-film equation as an overdamped evolution equation has a gradient flow structure, the informal implementation of the fluctuation-dissipation principle is straightforward. In this paper, we work out that the concept of Dirichlet forms and the related construction of Markov processes are tailor-made for this type of overdamped continuum evolution with thermal noise. However, the concept of Dirichlet forms relies on the availability of a Gibbsian equilibrium measure, which, in case of the thin-film equation, limits the treatment to the $(1+1)$-dimensional case. By means of Dirichlet form theory, we obtain the existence and uniqueness of the evolution of laws on configuration space. We show that the regularity of the realizations of this Markov process matches the heuristics. In a simplified situation with a Gaussian reference measure and a non-degenerate mobility function, we characterize it as what is called an energy solution. The latter provides a pathwise decomposition of the driving forces into a deterministic and a thermal one, which was the starting point. Applying the same techniques in the spatially discretized setting proposed in [Math. Comp. 92 (2023), 1931--1976], we obtain the same results uniformly in the discretization parameter. In particular, Galerkin as well as spectral approximations of the stochastic thin-film equation are shown to be uniformly tight in optimal topologies. In the simplified setting, we also prove Mosco convergence of the associated Dirichlet forms and thereby obtain convergence of these approximations.
item.dc:creator: Benjamin Gess, Felix Otto, Max Sauerbrey

item.title: Delocalized region of bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.42088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider bipartite Erd\H{o}s-R\'enyi graphs $\mathbb{G}(n, p, d/\sqrt{np})$ with two parts of sizes $n$ and $p$, respectively, and edge probability $d/\sqrt{pn}$. We show that for $d > b_* \log (n+p)$ all eigenvectors of its adjacency matrix, with eigenvalues away from zero, are delocalized with high probability. The threshold $b_*$ is an explicit function of the size ratio $n/p$ and optimal for eigenvector delocalization near the spectral edges. Our results extend to bulk eigenvectors down to the optimal threshold $d\geq \mathcal{D}\sqrt{\log (n+p)}$ for a constant $\mathcal D \geq 1$. In the supercritical scale $d \gg \log (n+p)$ we show that all eigenvectors are delocalized. Our results also hold for sparse rectangular random matrices with independent entries.
item.dc:creator: Johannes Alt, Serafina Wald

item.title: Band Random Graphs: Connectivity, Geometry, and Transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.42107v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G(n,p,m)$ be the random subgraph of the cycle power $C_n^m$ obtained by retaining each edge independently with probability $p$. We study connectivity, component geometry, and random walks throughout the regime $\log n\ll m<n/2$. We prove that $p\sim(\log n)/(2m)$ is a sharp threshold for connectivity. If $n(1-p)^{2m}\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)$, then the number of isolated vertices converges to $\mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda)$, and with high probability every other vertex lies in a single component $C_1$. In particular, the connectivity probability converges to $e^{-\lambda}$. The component $C_1$ contains a cyclic chain of connected sets occupying all but an $o(1)$ fraction of each consecutive block of length $\asymp m$, with $\Theta(m\log n)$ edges between consecutive sets. Its diameter has order $n/m+\log n/\log\log n$ with high probability. For every fixed $c>1$, uniformly over $p\geq c\log n/(2m)$, the lazy-walk spectral gap is asymptotic in probability to that of $C_n^m$. In the same range, the mean hitting time of simple random walk satisfies, uniformly over distinct $x,y$, $$ H_G(x,y)=\frac{2|E(G)|}{d_G(y)} +\frac{r_{xy}(n-r_{xy})}{\kappa_m} +o_{\mathrm{Prob}}\left(n+\frac{n^2}{m^2}\right), $$ where $r_{xy}$ is cyclic distance between vertices $x$ and $y$, $d_G(z)$ is the degree of vertex $z$ and $\kappa_m=(m+1)(2m+1)/6$. Thus, for this random graph model, connectivity has the Erd\H{o}s--R\'enyi asymptotics with $2m$ possible neighbours, while distances, relaxation, and hitting times retain the geometry of the underlying cycle.
item.dc:creator: Shantanav Chakraborty, Kyle Luh, Rudransh Pratap Singh

item.title: Fluctuation bounds for rotationally invariant first-passage percolation
item.description: arXiv:2610.42124v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that in rotationally invariant first-passage percolation on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with $d\geq2$, the passage time $T_n$ over a distance $n$ satisfies $\mathbb{E}[\exp(|T_n-\mu n|/n^{\frac{1}{2}(1-\varepsilon)})]\leq C$ for some $\varepsilon>0$, where $\mu$ is the time constant. This implies that its variance is at most a constant times $n^{1-\varepsilon}$, the bound that Basu, Sidoravicius and Sly proved in the planar case. As in their work, our argument is an induction on the scale, but in place of their proof that the geodesic is chaotic, we use the averaging argument of Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm together with a logarithmic improvement of the Efron-Stein inequality due to Bena\"im and Rossignol.
item.dc:creator: Scott Armstrong, Ahmed Bou-Rabee

item.title: Commutativity in a Poincar\'e-Type Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.07248v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study a Poincar\'e-type inequality for Gaussian measures restricted to origin-symmetric convex sets. The inequality arises from the second variation at $t=0$ of the function $t\longmapsto \gamma_{\Sigma}\left(e^{tA}K\right)$, where $\Sigma$ and $A$ are symmetric matrices. The relevance of this function comes from Saroglou's reformulation of the log-Brunn--Minkowski conjecture. We show that $\Sigma$ and $A$ commute if and only if the inequality holds for every box of the form $UD B_\infty^n$, where $U$ is orthogonal and $D$ is diagonal. In the non-commuting case, this yields counterexamples for orthogonal boxes whose axes can be chosen arbitrarily close to the coordinate axes. We also show that the inequality holds when $K$ is unconditional with respect to an eigenbasis of $\Sigma$ and $A$ is an arbitrary symmetric matrix.
item.dc:creator: Pavlos Kalantzopoulos

item.title: A law of the iterated logarithm for random multiplicative functions on integers with a large prime factor
item.description: arXiv:2610.40707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $f$ be a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on the squarefree integers. We investigate the almost sure fluctuations of the restricted sum $M^{>}(x)=\sum_{n\le x;~ P(n)>x^{1/2}}f(n)$, where $P(n)$ is the largest prime factor of $n$. With $Q(x)$ being the conditional variance of $M^{>}(x)$ given the values of $f$ at primes not exceeding $x^{1/2}$, we prove that, almost surely, the upper and lower limits of $M^{>}(x)(2Q(x)\log\log Q(x))^{-1/2}$ as $x\to\infty$ are $1$ and $-1$, respectively. Furthermore, it is shown that the almost sure cluster set of the normalized sum is $[-1,1]$.
item.dc:creator: Dariusz Buraczewski, Alexander Iksanov

item.title: Learning Finite-Memory Binary Sources
item.description: arXiv:2610.40845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating biased finite-memory sources from a single trajectory is a fundamental problem with practical impact, for example in estimating entropy for cryptography. We study order-$d$ binary sources whose conditional probabilities have bias at most $\epsilon$, and establish *sharp* sample complexity bounds: relative accuracy $\gamma$ with confidence $1-\delta$ needs $\gamma^{-2}\,(\tfrac12-\epsilon)^{-d}\,(\log d+\log\tfrac1\delta)$ samples up to constants depending on $\epsilon$, with matching upper and lower bounds and no dependence on mixing time or spectral gap. The proof rests on a sharp bound on expected hitting times of the sliding-window (de Bruijn) chain, which stay of order $1/\pi(w)$ uniformly in $d$ exactly when $\epsilon<\tfrac3{10}$, and on majorization of the window masses by those of independent biased coins. Applied to published entropy-source validations, the bounds show that their trace lengths may be underpowered: $10^6$ bits cannot resolve all transitions of an $8$-bit model to better than about $4.5\%$ relative error.
item.dc:creator: Maciej Skorski

item.title: Basis statistics for phylogenetic tree shape: tree balance formulas beyond expectations
item.description: arXiv:2610.40894v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Summary statistics that measure the shapes of phylogenetic trees contributed to quantitatively understanding evolutionary processes. Among phylogenetic summary statistics, the tree balance indices have been designed to capture intuitive notions of balance or imbalance in trees. Here, we characterize the tree balance indices in terms of basis statistics, mapping the exponentially large space of rooted, binary, unlabeled trees to lower-dimensional spaces. We observe that many tree balance indices can be represented in terms of linear functions of these low-dimensional spaces, enabling us to compute exact formulas for the means, variances, and covariances of many balance indices under the Yule--Harding model. The new framework recapitulates existing formulas for the expectations of 8 indices: Sackin index, average leaf depth, total cophenetic index, $\hat{s}$-shape statistic, Colless index, corrected Colless index, quadratic Colless index, and rooted quartet index for binary trees. It produces new formulas for the expectations of 9 additional indices: equal weights Colless index, total $I$ index, total $I'$ index, Rogers $J$ index, total internal path length, total path length, average vertex depth, stairs1 index, and stairs2 index. Moreover, the framework also allows us to calculate the exact variance of all 17 indices that are represented by the bases as well as the covariance and correlation for all $\binom{17}{2} = 136$ pairs among the 17 indices.
item.dc:creator: Daniel J. Bauman, Noah A. Rosenberg

item.title: Lengths of closed geodesics on random non-compact hyperbolic surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.41002v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the asymptotic distribution of the number of primitive, closed geodesics on Weil-Petersson random hyperbolic surfaces with genus $g$ and $n(g)$ cusps, under various growth rates of $n(g)$ as $g\to\infty$. We prove that the limiting distribution is Poisson with parameter depending explicitly on the limit of $n(g)^2/g$. This work is inspired by that of Mirzakhani and Petri's on closed surfaces and Hide and Thomas when $g$ is fixed. Our proof relies on first order expansions for Weil-Petersson moduli space volumes in the $n(g)/g\to 0$ regime. We also obtain some new existence results for small Laplacian eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Malo Gatignol, Joe Thomas

item.title: When can Optimally Trained Transformers Achieve Near-Lossless Token Prediction for non-Markovian Data?
item.description: arXiv:2610.41038v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: There exists little mathematical theory explaining why Transformer architectures are empirically successful even for non-Markovian data. To this end, this paper studies next-token prediction via stochastic optimal control theoretically trained Transformers for such sources, where we consider either stationary and ergodic non-Markovian sources or those which are hidden Markov models of some finite order (possibly non-stationary). In either case, we first obtain error bounds via finite models with finite window approximations. For stationary ergodic sources, the resulting error is bounded by an entropy gap; for $N$th order Markovian sources, it decays at an exponential rate $\alpha^{\lfloor M/N\rfloor}$, where $M$ is the window length and $\alpha$ is determined by filter stability (and the Dobrushin coefficients of the transition and measurement kernels). We then construct a Transformer of depth $M+1$, one head per layer, realizing the truncated filter, and we optimally train it with stochastic control developed in earlier work, which rigorously returns a near optimal Transformer. In particular, we show that for a non-Markovian source, either under stationarity and ergodicity for general models or under filter stability for hidden Markov models, an optimally trained Transformer has arbitrarily small performance error with increasing context length, data, and approximation refinement. Numerical studies accompany the theory.
item.dc:creator: Ka\u{g}an Akman, Jake Feldman Starosta, Naci Saldi, Serdar Y\"uksel

item.title: Variance Bounds and Strict Log-Concavity for Forest Coronas
item.description: arXiv:2610.41102v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the size of a random independent set in every nonempty forest has variance strictly smaller than its mean at common activity $0<t\le1$. A rooted quadratic reserve gives quantitative forms of this inequality. Mean matching transfers the bounds to fixed-weight canonical completion laws, and exact binomial moments prove strict log-concavity for every forest corona and every well-covered forest. The stronger factorial normalization $((m-j)!i_j)_{j=0}^m$ is strictly log-concave; we give explicit coefficient margins, terminal sharpness, one-less smoothing, and the exact universal three-index binomial ULC prefix. An exact attachment argument doubles the rooted reserve for every nontrivial unweighted tree. For a single marked root, a square reserve holds through $\Theta=\tfrac12e^{3-2W(1/e)}$ and for every positive mark at roots of degree at most four. A stronger reserve holds through mark $15/14$. These estimates yield marked clique, adjacent-pair, and repulsive two-piece variance bounds with fixed-weight canonical transfer. Finally, arbitrary positive site activities in $[3t/4,t]$ satisfy a uniform rooted reserve on every forest. This proves strict log-concavity for weighted forest coronas with compatible base marks. An explicit weighted-star obstruction shows why an unrestricted heterogeneous extension is impossible. Complete proofs are included, together with the required classical graph characterization and variance comparison.
item.dc:creator: Vadim E. Levit

item.title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.41595v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.
item.dc:creator: Kamran Arora, Federico Cornalba, Ana Djurdjevac

item.title: Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs
item.description: arXiv:2610.41735v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+\Theta_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it. We establish explicit upper and lower bounds on the surplus. The upper bound is obtained by counting common cores of minimum degree at least two, while the lower bound is established using spanning factors consisting of cycles of the same logarithmic length. For the special case $d=2$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n-(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))\log n$. The additional overlap achievable is also studied by rotating aligned Hamilton cycles, using a contiguity argument. As a by-product, we determine the asymptotic maximum overlap between unions of independent random perfect matchings under cyclic shifts.
item.dc:creator: Andrea D'Ascenzo, Riccardo Michielan

item.title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
item.description: arXiv:2610.41802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models. Our result matches the recovery guarantees of non-backtracking spectral methods while using Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices. To do this, we identify recursive formulas for the negative outlier eigenvalues and show that their eigenspaces have nonvanishing overlap with the corresponding planted eigenspaces. The proof constructs approximate eigenvectors from the planted labels on the limiting Poisson tree, with weights given by its Green's function, and transfers these approximations to the finite graph.
item.dc:creator: Dingding Dong, Theo McKenzie

item.title: Existence of the thermodynamic limit for the Hopfield model
item.description: arXiv:2610.41938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the quenched pressure of the Hopfield model with $K\sim\alpha N$ i.i.d. symmetric Rademacher patterns has a thermodynamic limit at every load $\alpha\in(0,\infty)$, finite inverse temperature and uniform external field, with no replica-symmetry, order-parameter concentration or non-condensation hypothesis required. The limit is the supremum over $r$ of limiting pressures of mixed models with $r$ binary patterns in a Gaussian bulk. Via the Hubbard--Stratonovich representation we extract the finitely many patterns whose hidden coordinates exceed $\delta\sqrt N$; a collective interpolation replaces the other binary patterns by Gaussian ones with error $O(\delta^2)$ uniform in the volume, and convex concentration on the discrete cube controls the disorder-dependent choice of retained patterns. For the mixed models we prove a Gaussian hidden-spin truncation bound uniform in the volume and in an arbitrary Ising potential, and convergence for Gaussian bulks with finitely many site-field types, reducing to results of Ho and of Chen, Ho and Issa on non-convex vector spin glasses with compact spins. For Gaussian patterns we give an alternative proof of the existence result announced by Camilli, Contucci and Mingione, extended to a uniform field and an extra binary pattern. In both cases the pressure has exponentially small deviation probabilities and converges a.s.; internal energy and entropy converge wherever the limit is differentiable. An extra binary Mattis pattern admits a scalar variational reduction. At zero field the Rademacher pressure dominates the Gaussian one with an extra binary pattern, which dominates the pure Gaussian one. No explicit formula is given. The proofs were generated through extensive interaction with the AI models Claude (Opus~5.5) and ChatGPT (Sol~6.1), based on the problem formulation and guidance of the authors.
item.dc:creator: Adriano Barra, Fabrizio Durante

item.title: Stochastic Rayleigh-Ritz Ascent: Global Linear Convergence under a Spectral Gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.42071v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider the adjoint-free random-plane iteration algorithm for finding the top eigenvector of a matrix proposed in (SIAM J. Matrix Anal. Appl. 47 (2026), 1349-1374). Unlike standard methods such as the power method or gradient descent, the above algorithm lacked linear convergence guarantees in the presence of a spectral gap. In this paper, we establish explicit spectral-gap-dependent global linear convergence rates in expectation, providing quantitative guarantees for the empirically observed convergence.
item.dc:creator: Jonas Bresch, Oleh Melnyk

item.title: Maximal Inequalities for Empirical Processes under General Mixing Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2402.11394v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper provides a bound for the supremum of sample averages over a class of functions for a general class of mixing stochastic processes with arbitrary mixing rates. Regardless of the speed of mixing, the bound is comprised of a concentration rate and a novel measure of complexity. The speed of mixing, however, affects the former quantity implying a phase transition. Fast mixing leads to the standard root-n concentration rate, while slow mixing leads to a slower concentration rate whose speed depends on the mixing structure. Our findings are applied to obtain new Glivenko-Cantelli type results.
item.dc:creator: Demian Pouzo

item.title: Transition in the asymptotics of the joint degree distribution of uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs
item.description: arXiv:2503.05829v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the asymptotic joint degree distribution of uniformly chosen vertices in uniform recursive directed acyclic graphs, a natural generalization of random recursive trees. Here, a graph is built by adding vertices one-by-one and connecting each new vertex to $m\in\mathbb{N}$ uniformly selected vertices already present. Using a representation based on Kingman's coalescent, we establish a transition in the joint degree distribution at the threshold $(m+1)\log n$, arising from the interplay between geometric degree asymptotics and fluctuations in the coalescent construction. Our results extend previously known asymptotics toward this threshold and provide a unified description of the transition, including mixed regimes where prescribed degrees lie on different scales.
item.dc:creator: Rafael Engel

item.title: Co-evolving vertex and edge dynamics in dense graphs
item.description: arXiv:2504.06493v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a random graph in which vertices can have one of two possible colours. Each vertex switches its colour at a rate that is proportional to the number of vertices of the other colour to which it is connected by an edge. Each edge turns on or off according to a rate that depends on whether the vertices at its two endpoints have the same colour or not. We prove that, in the limit as the graph size tends to infinity and the graph becomes dense, the graph process converges, in a suitable path topology, to a limiting Markov process that lives on a certain subset of the space of coloured graphons. In the limit, the density of each vertex colour evolves according to a Fisher-Wright diffusion driven by the density of the edges, while the underlying edge connectivity structure evolves according to a stochastic flow whose drift depends on the densities of the two vertex colours.
item.dc:creator: Siva Athreya, Frank den Hollander, Adrian R\"ollin

item.title: Circular law for non-Hermitian block band matrices with slowly growing bandwidth
item.description: arXiv:2511.01744v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the empirical eigenvalue distribution for a class of non-Hermitian random block tridiagonal matrices $T$ with independent entries. The matrix has $n$ blocks on the diagonal and each block has size $\ell_n$, so the whole matrix has size $n\ell_n$. We assume that the nonzero entries are i.i.d. with mean 0, variance $(3\ell_n)^{-1}$ and having finite moments of all orders. We prove that when the entries have a bounded density, then whenever $\lim_{n\to\infty}\ell_n=\infty$ and $\ell_n=O(\operatorname{Poly}(n))$, the normalized empirical spectral distribution of $T$ converges almost surely to the circular law. The growing bandwidth condition $\lim _{n\to\infty}\ell_n=\infty$ is the optimal condition for the circular law with small bandwidth. This confirms the folklore conjecture that the circular law holds whenever the bandwidth increases with the dimension; earlier circular-law proofs required the delocalized regime $\ell_n\gg n$.
item.dc:creator: Yi Han

item.title: Distributional properties of first jump times of CBI processes with jump sizes in given Borel sets
item.description: arXiv:2512.04935v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive an expression for the joint distribution function of the first jump times of a continuous state and continuous time branching process with immigration (CBI process) with jump sizes in given Borel sets having finite total L\'evy measures, where by total L\'evy measure, we mean the sum of the measures appearing in the branching and immigration mechanisms of the CBI process in question. Our result generalizes a corresponding result of He and Li (2016), who considered this problem in case of a single Borel set having finite total L\'evy measure.
item.dc:creator: Matyas Barczy, Sandra Palau, Yao Xue

item.title: Lower and Upper Expected Hitting Times for Weighted Imprecise Markov Chains
item.description: arXiv:2603.16665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we extend hitting times for imprecise Markov chains to the framework of weighted imprecise Markov chains (WIMCs), in which each transition is associated with a strictly positive weight encoded by a matrix $W$. Given a convex set $\mathcal{T}$ of admissible transition matrices, we define lower and upper expected hitting times for WIMCs as the infimum and supremum of the (weighted) expected hitting times over $\mathcal{T}$, and we characterise these quantities as the unique solutions of nonlinear fixed-point equations. We show that any weighted hitting time problem can be transformed into an unweighted hitting time problem on an augmented state space, enabling the reuse of existing IMC theory and algorithms. In particular, we are able to adapt known iterative methods for the numerical computation of lower and upper hitting times for WIMCs.
item.dc:creator: Marco Sangalli, Thomas Krak

item.title: Relation between Hitting Times and Probabilities for Imprecise Markov Chains
item.description: arXiv:2603.16675v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the relation between hitting times and hitting probabilities in discrete-time imprecise Markov chains (IMCs). We define lower and upper hitting times and probabilities for IMCs whose set of transition matrices $\T$ is compact, convex, and has separately specified rows. Building on reachability-based partitions of the state space, we prove two key implications: (i) finiteness of the upper expected hitting time entails the lower hitting probability equals one, and (ii) finiteness of the lower expected hitting time entails the upper hitting probability equals one. We further show an equivalence: the upper expected hitting time is finite if and only if the lower hitting probability is one. Finally, by presenting a counterexample, we show that the converse of the second implication can fail.
item.dc:creator: Marco Sangalli, Erik Quaeghebeur, Thomas Krak

item.title: A Sharp Refinement of Samuels' Inequality via Cap Moves
item.description: arXiv:2608.22816v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $0\le \mu_1\le \mu_2 \le \cdots \le \mu_n$ and $\delta > 0$. Samuels' conjecture states that if $X_1,\dots,X_n$ are independent non-negative random variables with $\mathbb{E}[X_i] = \mu_i$, then $$ \mathbb{P}\left( \sum_{i=1}^n X_i < \delta + \sum_{i=1}^n \mu_i \right) \ge \min_{1\le i\le n} \prod_{j=i}^n \left(1-\frac{\mu_j}{\delta + \sum_{k=i}^n \mu_k}\right).$$ This conjecture was recently proved by Ling. In this note, we prove a refinement of Samuels' inequality via an operation called the \emph{cap move}. Our refined inequality is sharp, with equality attained for a strictly larger class of distributions than in the original inequality.
item.dc:creator: Yanjun Han, Zipei Nie

item.title: Strong Invariance Principle for Random Dirichlet Series
item.description: arXiv:2610.18353v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: It is shown that the random prime Dirichlet series $ X(s)=\sum_{p\in \mathcal{P}}\frac{\xi_p}{p^{s+1/2}} $ can be almost surely approximated by a Brownian motion, where $ \{\xi_p\}_{p\ge 1} $ are independent and identically distributed random variables with zero mean and finite variance, and $ \mathcal{P} $ is the set of prime numbers. As a consequence, the functional law of the iterated logarithm, limit laws of the iterated logarithm, and Chung's law of the iterated logarithm for $ X(s) $ are obtained. It is also shown that the random Dirichlet series $ Y(s)=\sum_{k=2}^{\infty} \frac{(\log k)^{\alpha}}{k^{s+1/2}} $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ admits the same approximation as $ X(s) $, and a direct relationship between $ X(s) $ and $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha=-1/2 $ is established. The strong invariance principle for $ Y(s) $ with $ \alpha>-1/2 $ is also obtained.
item.dc:creator: Li-Xin Zhang

item.title: The Berry--Esseen estimate in the Boolean central limit theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.39743v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We estimate the L\'evy distance to the symmetric Bernoulli distribution for normalized Boolean convolution powers of a probability measure with mean zero and variance one. If the absolute moment of order $r$ is finite, we obtain the upper bounds $o(n^{-(r-2)/6})$ for $2<r<5$ and $O(n^{-1/2})$ for $r\ge5$. The proof relies on an inequality that controls the L\'evy distance to the Bernoulli law by the values of the reciprocal Cauchy transform at two points. For each $r\ge2$, we also construct a single fixed distribution whose absolute moments are finite exactly up to order $r$, and show that the exponent $\min\{(r-2)/6,1/2\}$ cannot be improved. Under only a finite second moment assumption, the convergence can be arbitrarily slow.
item.dc:creator: Makoto Maejima, Noriyoshi Sakuma

item.title: General-purpose post-sampling reweighting method for multimodal target measures
item.description: arXiv:2602.12027v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When sampling multi-modal probability distributions, correctly estimating the relative probability of each mode, even when the modes have been discovered and locally sampled, remains challenging. We test a simple reweighting scheme designed for this situation, which consists in minimizing (in terms of weights) the Kullback-Leibler divergence of a weighted (regularized) empirical distribution of the samples with respect to the target measure. We show in a theoretical toy model that the convergence in terms of the number of samples follows the Monte Carlo rate. Numerical experiments on a variety of simple benchmarks are provided, exploring the effect of the ambient dimension, number of modes, number of samples and definition of the modes. We find that, particularly in the situation of interest with well-identified separated modes, the method is able to correct the error in the estimation from the initial sampling of the relative probabilities of the modes.
item.dc:creator: Pierre Monmarch\'e

item.title: Tackling the 6/49 Lottery and Debunking Common Myths with Probabilistic Methods and Combinatorial Designs
item.description: arXiv:2603.24170v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: At the end, the house always wins! This simple truth holds for all public games of chance. Nevertheless, since lotteries have existed, people have tried everything to give luck a helping hand. This article compares objective scientific approaches to tackle the 6/49 lottery: probabilistic methods and combinatorial designs. The mathematical models developed herein can be modified and applied to other lotteries. The newly constructed (49, 6, 5) covering design is introduced, which meets the Sch\"onheim bound. For lottery designs and for covering designs, a benchmark based on probabilistic methods is presented. It is demonstrated that common attempts to outwit the odds correspond to limitations of numbers to subsets, which disproportionately reduce the chances of winning.
item.dc:creator: Ralph St\"ommer

item.title: Structural identifiability of partially-observed stochastic processes: from single-particle trajectories to total particle density data
item.description: arXiv:2605.13504v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The increasing availability of experimental data has intensified interest in calibrating stochastic models, raising fundamental questions about parameter identifiability. Structural identifiability determines whether parameters can be uniquely recovered from idealised data, a prerequisite to allow for parameter estimation in real-world scenarios. However, there is a lack of methodologies generally applicable to analyse the structural identifiability of such stochastic processes. Therefore, we develop a methodology for a class of spatio-temporal stochastic processes. We investigate how structural identifiability depends on the type of available data, distinguishing between single-particle trajectories and total particle density measurements. For trajectory data, we use a particle-based description that explicitly represents single-particle dynamics. For population-level data, we derive a partial differential equation representation, that describes the evolution of total particle density, and apply a differential algebra approach, common to ordinary differential equation analysis. We further introduce Taylor-series-expansion and Fourier-transform approaches to study the initial condition. We apply our methodology to an example model with a specified class of initial conditions. We show that the model is globally structurally identifiable given infinitely many, infinitely long single-particle trajectories, but only locally structurally identifiable from total particle density data, demonstrating that parameter identifiability depends on the type of data available.
item.dc:creator: Arianna Ceccarelli, Alexander P. Browning, Ruth E. Baker
